Professional Engagement | Careers & Development

Connecting Students with Professional Bodies at Northumbria University's Built Environment Careers Fair

12 October 2026 · Northumbria University Students' Union, Newcastle upon Tyne · Completed

Event organiser: Northumbria University. Northumbria Construct's role: Participating organisation, sharing a joint stand with APM and CIOB.

Bringing Academia and Industry Closer Together

On 12 October 2026, Northumbria Construct participated in Northumbria University's Built Environment Careers Fair, sharing a stand with the Association for Project Management (APM) and the Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB).

The joint engagement marked an important milestone in Northumbria Construct's mission to bridge the gap between academia and the construction industry by helping students access professional networks, development opportunities and pathways into their chosen careers.

Throughout the event, students engaged with representatives to explore professional membership opportunities, including suitable membership grades, the benefits of joining professional institutions and the resources available to support their professional development.

Discussions also highlighted opportunities for networking, volunteering, continued professional learning and progression towards professional recognition.

Strengthening Professional Engagement

For Northumbria Construct, participating alongside two leading professional institutions provided an opportunity to demonstrate how collaboration between universities, student-led initiatives and professional bodies can help students navigate the construction industry's professional landscape.

The engagement reinforced Northumbria Construct's role as an intermediary, connecting students with established professional institutions and signposting opportunities that complement their academic development.

We extend our appreciation to Northumbria University for organising the Careers Fair and to the APM and CIOB for their collaboration and continued commitment to supporting emerging construction and project management professionals.

title: Bridging industry and education at Gateshead College
excerpt: Northumbria Construct supported CIOB North East Tomorrow’s Leaders at Gateshead College, connecting approximately 40 students with industry professionals and university volunteers. Interactive careers discussions, the BRIC pilot and a building challenge brought career pathways, collaboration and practical learning together.
image_alt: Industry participants and volunteers gathered at Gateshead College for the professional engagement day
body_html:
Activity · Newcastle Hub

7 October 2026 · Gateshead College, UK · Completed

Northumbria Construct supported CIOB North East Tomorrow’s Leaders in delivering a Professional Engagement Day for approximately 40 college students, connecting them with industry professionals and university volunteers.

Careers brought to life

Using the CIOB Think Construction Toolkit, the team adapted Inspiring a Career in Construction and Construction Myths vs Facts into interactive presentations and discussions. Students explored the breadth of construction roles and routes through higher education, apprenticeships and practical experience.

The day piloted BRIC — Build Routes Into Construction with its intended audience. Students built and discussed credible career pathways; practical feedback highlighted opportunities to refine gameplay and simplify instructions.

Collaboration, creativity and teamwork

Working in eight teams, students took part in the Iconic Building Challenge using spaghetti and marshmallows. Creations included the Leaning Tower of Pasta and Marshmallows and St. Greggs Basilica. The exercise encouraged communication, problem-solving and teamwork while translating ideas into physical structures.

Volunteers making a difference

Northumbria Construct contributed to planning, volunteer mobilisation, stakeholder coordination and interactive activity delivery. Callum O’Connor led the volunteer team, alongside Vemula Sai Praneeth, Finn Mulholland, Aditya Shetty, Mayuri Shinde and Collins Tamunotonye.

We thank CIOB North East Tomorrow’s Leaders, Gateshead College, participating industry professionals and every volunteer. The event built on Bridge the Gap’s lessons about making professional networks, career information and participation more accessible.

Activity · Newcastle Hub

23 September 2026 · Northumbria University, Newcastle upon Tyne · Completed

Northumbria Construct joined the Northumbria University Students’ Union Societies Fair, welcoming new and returning students from different disciplines to explore professional development, industry engagement and collaborative learning.

Committee members and volunteers discussed networking, volunteering, site visits, seminars and the value of joining professional communities while studying. Students were introduced to APM, CIOB and ICE; support from APM enabled the stand to offer student membership information and resources.

Continuing the Bridge the Gap mission

The fair sustained the founding project’s ambition to improve construction career awareness and strengthen student–industry engagement. We welcomed new members and students interested in contributing to projects, practical learning and professional networks.

Our thanks go to Callum O’Connor, Zaw Min Htet and Aditya Shetty for representing Northumbria Construct, and to Michelle Littlemore and Robin Carter-Evans for facilitating APM student membership resources. We thank Northumbria Students’ Union for organising the fair and every student who visited the stand.

title: Quayside Heritage Walk — Exploring Newcastle’s Built Heritage
excerpt: Explore the architectural and industrial history of Newcastle and Gateshead through a guided Quayside walk led by Aditya T. Shetty. Discover historic buildings, infrastructure, heritage conservation and regeneration while connecting with students and built-environment enthusiasts. Participation is free and open to everyone.
image_alt: Northumbria Construct Quayside Heritage Walk A5 poster: Friday 23 October, 4:00–6:00 PM, exploring Newcastle’s industry and regeneration via Millennium Bridge, BALTIC, Tyne Bridge, The Close and Sandhill.
body_html:

Explore the architectural and industrial history of Newcastle and Gateshead through a guided walk along the Quayside.

Ask about participating →

Heritage, industry and regeneration

From historic merchant houses and industrial infrastructure to contemporary regeneration and adaptive reuse, the walk examines how the built environment reflects the city’s changing economic and social history.

Participants will explore landmarks including the Gateshead Millennium Bridge, BALTIC Centre for Contemporary Art, Tyne Bridge, The Close and Sandhill.

The event provides an informal opportunity to learn about heritage conservation, construction history and urban regeneration while connecting with fellow students and built-environment enthusiasts.

The walk is open to everyone. Optional social drinks may follow.

Meet your walk lead

Aditya T. Shetty

Aditya T. Shetty is a built-environment professional with a specialist interest in the sustainable restoration and conservation of historic buildings. His work explores conservation decision-making, historic fabric preservation and the balance between heritage protection and contemporary sustainability requirements.

In June 2026, Aditya participated as a panellist in the Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB) discussion, EPCs & Proposed Changes: What They Mean for Listed Buildings in England, contributing perspectives on sustainable retrofit, conservation and historic-building performance.

Related professional engagement: CIOB panel discussion ↗

title: People-Led Digital Twins for Preventive Conservation of Built Heritage Assets
excerpt: Explore a University of Bath doctoral research opportunity bringing together digital twins, structural health monitoring and explainable artificial intelligence for built heritage conservation. Home and overseas applicants may apply subject to programme requirements. Funding is competitive, and applications close on 29 November 2026.

Explore how digital technologies can support the conservation and management of historic buildings and infrastructure. This University of Bath PhD investigates people-led digital twins for preventive conservation of built heritage assets.

The research brings together structural health monitoring, sensor data, inspection records, interactive visualisation and explainable artificial intelligence to inform conservation decisions.

Human-in-the-loop approaches keep engineers, conservation specialists and other stakeholders involved in interpreting information, assessing asset conditions and deciding when to intervene. The project supports professional judgement in managing historic structures.

Who might be interested?

  • Built heritage conservation and restoration
  • Structural engineering and asset management
  • Digital twins and BIM
  • Structural health monitoring
  • Artificial intelligence and explainable decision-support systems
  • Sustainable management of historic infrastructure

Competitive funding

The project is competing for a studentship under the University of Bath's Faculty of Engineering and Design. Successful studentship recipients are expected to receive tuition-fee support, a maintenance stipend and a training-support allowance, subject to the published funding conditions. Funding is competitive and an award is not guaranteed.

title: Bridge the Gap
excerpt: The founding Bridge the Gap project investigated barriers to student engagement with the construction industry through research, stakeholder engagement, interviews and educational outreach. Its learning about opportunity visibility, understanding and accessibility shaped a continuing programme and the establishment of Northumbria Construct.
image_alt: Bridge the Gap project team standing together at a professional event
body_html:
Project · Organisation-wide · Founding initiative

The project that led to the creation of Northumbria Construct.

Project overview

Developed during the Association for Project Management (APM) Project Management Challenge, the project investigated why many students struggled to engage effectively with the construction industry despite the wealth of opportunities available through universities, employers and professional institutions.

Using structured project management methodologies, the project combined research, stakeholder engagement, industry interviews, storytelling and educational outreach to better understand the barriers preventing meaningful participation.

The findings demonstrated that the primary challenge was not the absence of opportunity, but the lack of visibility, understanding and accessibility.

Recognising that these challenges extended beyond the competition itself, the project team transformed Bridge the Gap into a continuing programme of professional engagement, leading to the establishment of Northumbria Construct.

Project objectives

  • Investigate barriers affecting student engagement with industry.
  • Strengthen collaboration between academia and the built environment.
  • Improve awareness of professional pathways and career opportunities.
  • Encourage participation in professional institutions, volunteering and networking.
  • Deliver sustainable educational benefits beyond the project.

Learning that shaped the organisation

The project found that opportunities needed greater visibility, understanding and accessibility. Its transition into Northumbria Construct carried that learning into a continuing engagement programme.

Key activities

  • Research and stakeholder surveys
  • Industry interviews and professional storytelling
  • Educational seminars and outreach activities
  • University, institution and industry collaboration
  • Innovative stakeholder engagement approaches
  • Transition planning for long-term sustainability

Project outcomes

  • Better understanding of engagement challenges
  • Evidence-based recommendations
  • Innovative engagement frameworks
  • A sustainable programme of professional engagement
  • Demonstrated benefit realisation through transition

title: Oxford-Style Debate
excerpt: A structured debate brought students, academics and industry professionals together to examine readiness for professional practice. image_alt: Participants gathered for a group photograph after the Northumbria Construct Oxford-Style Debate
body_html:
Project · Newcastle Hub

A structured debate that turned discussion into practical recommendations and new opportunities.

Debate motion
“Universities Are Failing to Prepare Graduates for Industry.”

Project overview

The project brought together participants, academics and industry professionals to examine the responsibilities of universities, individuals, employers and professional institutions in preparing graduates for professional practice.

Audience feedback and recommendations were analysed and compiled into a formal report presented to stakeholders within Northumbria University Experiential Learning Team and the Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB).

Recommendations included clearer communication around opportunities and improved signposting of Personal Protective Equipment availability for construction site visits. These actions contributed to increased participation in subsequent CIOB site visits.

Planning, delivery and learning

The managed engagement brought together participants, academics and industry professionals, collected audience feedback and presented recommendations to stakeholders. The delivery experience demonstrated the value of clearer opportunity communication and PPE signposting.

Version 1 of NorCon Projects was tested through the project, including briefs, activity planning, Gantt charts, progress tracking, stakeholder coordination, RACI matrices, dashboards and reporting. Explore its applications.

Objectives

Meaningful dialogue

Create collaboration, evaluate industry readiness and produce evidence-based recommendations.

Activities

Structured engagement

Plan the debate, collect stakeholder feedback and present findings to institutional partners.

Outcomes

Measurable benefits

Improved communication, better PPE signposting and increased participation in CIOB site visits.

title: BRIC — Build Routes Into Construction
excerpt: BRIC is an interactive educational card game helping students explore credible routes into construction careers. Teams combine qualifications, apprenticeships and practical experience, adapt to challenges and discuss progression. A Gateshead College pilot is informing clearer instructions, refined gameplay and future educational development.
image_alt: Northumbria Construct BRIC card game overview showing collaborative career pathway exploration
body_html:
Innovation · Developed by Northumbria Construct

Explore. Discover. Plan. Progress.

One industry. Many careers. Multiple pathways.

An interactive educational card game helping students and aspiring professionals discover, construct and defend their own routes into construction and the built environment.

BRIC combines career exploration, collaborative problem-solving and strategic decision-making. It connects qualifications, apprenticeships, work experience and professional development in a hands-on learning experience.

Career guidance can make it difficult to see how different routes connect. BRIC encourages participants to recognise transferable skills and explore alternatives: your qualification is a starting point, not your destination.

How BRIC works

Teams use colour-coded cards to build credible pathways from a starting point to a construction career. Five interconnected elements guide the journey:

  1. START — Where are you now?

    Begin with a qualification, apprenticeship, technical education or experience in another industry.

  2. ROUTE — How could you get there?

    Combine qualifications, apprenticeships, employment and practical experience into a realistic pathway.

  3. DESTINATION — Where do you want to go?

    Explore roles such as Construction Project Manager, BIM Manager, Structural Engineer, Quantity Surveyor and Sustainability Specialist.

  4. WILDCARD — What if circumstances change?

    Adapt to constraints such as earning while studying or pursuing a career without attending university full-time, and justify your choices.

  5. PROGRESSION — What comes next?

    Consider continuing professional development, leadership, specialisation and professional recognition.

The challenge is to show that multiple credible routes can lead to the same career, through discussion, teamwork and friendly competition.

From concept to classroom

BRIC first appeared at the CIOB North East Tomorrow’s Leaders Professional Engagement Day at Gateshead College on 7 October 2026. The initial physical edition included 50 cards per team, with career destinations, educational pathways, locally relevant Gateshead College opportunities and discussion challenges.

The pilot provided practical insights into student engagement, gameplay and instruction clarity. These are informing refinements to gameplay, simpler instructions and the learning experience. Explore the event and photographs →

Learning through exploration

BRIC is designed to support career awareness, understanding of alternative pathways, critical thinking, teamwork, communication and career confidence. For educators and professionals, it offers a structured way to begin career conversations and connect learning with real occupations.

Designed to evolve

Development continues following the first physical pilot. Cards can be tailored to institutions, qualification systems, occupational specialisms and regional opportunities. Northumbria Construct is exploring stronger educational content, refinements to the physical game and potential digital adaptations. These are future possibilities rather than released products.

Interested in educational workshops, further testing or collaboration? Explore BRIC with us →

title: NorCon Projects
excerpt: NorCon Projects is a lightweight project management application for small teams delivering social-impact projects. Successive versions have been tested through the Oxford-Style Debate and Gateshead engagement day, bringing planning, coordination, reporting, accountability and sustainability tracking together through iterative development and practical learning.
body_html:
NorCon Projects · In development

Developing, testing and improving through real-world application.

A lightweight project management application for small teams delivering social-impact projects.

NorCon Projects brings planning, coordination, progress monitoring and reporting into one environment, with embedded accountability, change control and sustainability tracking. Its aim is structured project governance without unnecessary complexity.

Northumbria Construct tests successive versions on real projects, using practical experience to inform continuous improvement.

Two projects. Two versions. One evolving solution.

Version 1

Northumbria Construct Oxford-Style Debate

The first application tested core capabilities: project briefs and activity planning; Gantt charts and progress tracking; stakeholder coordination and RACI matrices; project dashboards and reporting.

Explore the debate project →

Version 2

Volunteering at the Gateshead College engagement day

Building on the first application, the delivery environment introduced integrated project baselines and governance; risk, issue and change control; benefits and value management; sustainability performance tracking; enhanced reporting and project controls.

Explore the planning and delivery project →

Develop → Test → Learn → Improve

Real projects help evaluate functionality, identify limitations and refine features and workflows. Each iteration informs our understanding of small teams’ delivery challenges and how digital tools can support them without unnecessary administration.

Our goal is to make good project management more accessible. NorCon Projects remains in iterative development and testing; no public release date is announced.
